title: How to Fix the Single Shared Trace Log: Automatic Recording, Hardening, and Hygiene

tldr.content:
Fix automatic recording by emitting traces from code seams that already run, not by asking the model to remember: supply a built-in trace lifecycle hook to the orchestrator (its 8 `hooks?.run(...)` sites fire every run but are inert because production never passes `lifecycleHooks`), emit a loop-checkpoint trace from the csm-build/csm-plan/csm-review loop CLIs, keep wt-session, and add a `scripts/trace.mjs` CLI + `make trace` for explicit/instruction-led use that `AGENTS.md` names exactly.

Harden the path: contain a relative configured `traceLogPath` under the repo root (an escape currently writes outside the repo).

Delete the unreachable per-run fallback; document/archive the old logs (gitignored, no auto-migration).

Residual: agent-composed steps that invoke no CLI are only covered by an optional host opencode plugin (`tool.execute.after`/`event`/`permission.ask`); Jev advisory agrees the in-repo seams are the right mechanism but rates sufficiency 0.40 with that exact gap at 0.94.

executiveSummary.content:
Question: how should the partially-implemented single shared trace log be fixed so actions and decisions actually land in one log?

```text

gap: only wt-session writes; recordDecision unused; no hook

fix A (in-repo, deterministic): orchestrator lifecycle-hook trace + loop-CLI checkpoints + wt-session + trace CLI + git pre-commit

fix B (hardening): contain relative configured path; docs for invalid-layer default

fix C (hygiene): delete dead fallback; archive old logs (no auto-migrate)

fix D (optional, host): opencode plugin tool.execute.after/event covers agent-only steps

```

The strongest seam is the orchestrator lifecycle hook runner: `csm-orchestrate/lib/index.mjs` already calls `hooks?.run(...)` at eight points per run [ref-index], so registering a built-in trace hook makes recording deterministic for orchestrated runs with no new call sites [ref-lifecycle-hooks]. The three loop CLIs add per-cycle coverage [ref-loop-guard][ref-loop-evaluator][ref-loop-closure]. Prototypes confirm both append redacted UTC JSONL [ref-prototypes].

The honest residual is agent-composed work that invokes no CLI; only a host plugin closes it [ref-plugin-api]. Jev advisory agrees the in-repo seams are correct (0.98) and names that residual (0.94) [ref-jev-review].

detailSections.content:
## D1. Automatic recording via the orchestrator lifecycle hooks

`createLifecycleHookRunner` validates hook names (worker-start/stop, task-create/complete, tool-exec, checkpoint, cancel) and runs handlers synchronously in a try/catch, so a throwing hook is skipped, never fatal [ref-lifecycle-hooks]. `index.mjs` already calls `hooks?.run(...)` at :266, :295, :1011, :1041, :1042, :1048, :1490, :1497 [ref-index]. Production passes no hooks (`run-orchestrator.mjs:898-942` omits `lifecycleHooks`), so the handlers are inert [ref-run-orchestrator]. Fix: add `csm-orchestrate/lib/trace-hooks.mjs` exporting `createTraceLifecycleHooks` that maps each hook name to a handler calling `appendTrace`/`recordDecision` (fire-and-forget with a pending-set + `flush()`), and pass it from the driver.

```mermaid

flowchart LR

  orch[orchestrate run] --> hooks{lifecycle hooks}

  hooks -->|task-create/complete, checkpoint, tool-exec| trace[appendTrace -> shared log]

  hooks -->|verdict/route| dec[recordDecision -> shared log]

```

## D2. Deterministic sink CLI for explicit/instruction-led use

Add `scripts/trace.mjs` (`action|decision|--stdin`) that validates and writes through `trace-log.mjs` (required fields, UTC ts, redaction, bounded single write) and a `make trace` target; name the exact command in `AGENTS.md`. Prototype: the wrapper wrote 2 lines (kinds action+decision), UTC, and redacted a synthetic `API_KEY=` value [ref-prototypes][ref-trace-log].

## D3. Path and config hardening

`repoLogPath` uses `path.join(mainRoot, configured)` and `join` normalizes `..`, so a relative configured value escapes the repo (prototype reproduced `/tmp/...`) [ref-repo-state][ref-prototypes]. Contain relative values under the main root and fall an escape back to the in-repo default; correct `docs/action-traces-and-cleanup.md` (which currently says a relative value stays under the repo root) [ref-docs-traces]. The invalid-layer-to-in-repo-default path already exists; document it [ref-trace-config].

## D4. Old-log disposition

`.agents/logs/*` is gitignored, so migrating is an operator action, and re-concatenation duplicates lines [ref-gitignore][ref-docs-traces]. Document both the old `<git-common-dir>/csm/logs/trace.jsonl` and the legacy per-run file, with exact list/concatenate commands; optionally add a read-only legacy lister that never mutates.

## D5. Dead code

`appendTrace` and `repoLogPath` load in the same `try` and the `appendTrace === null` guard returns first, so the per-run fallback branch is unreachable [ref-wt-session]; delete it and fix the stale run-id comment.

## D6. Host plugin (optional, outside the repo)

opencode's plugin API exposes `tool.execute.after`/`tool.execute.before`, `event`, and `permission.ask` [ref-plugin-api]; the host has `@opencode-ai/plugin` installed but no plugin configured. A plugin that appends an action trace per tool call and a decision trace per permission would cover agent-composed steps the in-repo seams cannot. This is host configuration, not a repo deliverable; document it and keep it opt-in.

## D7. Phased fix

```text

P1 (in-repo, high value): orchestrator trace hook + loop-CLI checkpoints + trace CLI/make + AGENTS naming + delete dead fallback

P2 (hardening): relative-path containment + docs + tests

P3 (hygiene): document/archive old logs; optional legacy lister

P4 (optional, host): opencode plugin for agent-only steps

```

recommendation.content:
Make recording automatic where code already runs, and make the remaining manual path one exact command. Concretely:

P1 - (a) add `csm-orchestrate/lib/trace-hooks.mjs` (`createTraceLifecycleHooks`) and pass it from `scripts/run-orchestrator.mjs`; (b) emit a `loop-checkpoint` action trace from the csm-build/csm-plan/csm-review loop CLIs; (c) keep `wt-session`; (d) add `scripts/trace.mjs` + `make trace` and name that command in `AGENTS.md`; (e) delete the unreachable fallback in `wt-session.mjs`.

P2 - contain a relative configured `traceLogPath` under the repo root (escape falls back to the in-repo default) and correct the docs; add tests for the escape and for the invalid-layer default.

P3 - document/archive the old `<git-common-dir>` log and the legacy per-run file; do not auto-migrate; optional read-only lister.

P4 - optionally provide a host opencode plugin (`tool.execute.after`/`event`/`permission.ask`) to cover agent-composed steps; keep it opt-in and out of the repo.

Confidence: HIGH on P1-P3 (code seams, prototypes, and the challenger all converge). MEDIUM on how much of the residual the host plugin actually closes, since agent-composed steps are inherently outside the repo's control. What would change the answer: evidence that the orchestrator is rarely the execution path (then the loop CLIs and git hook carry more weight), or a decision to require a host plugin as the primary mechanism.

unverifiedClaims.content:
U1. partially-supported - How completely a host opencode plugin would cover agent-composed steps; the plugin API exists but was not exercised (installing a plugin changes host config, out of scope).

U2. unverified - Whether the orchestrator is the dominant execution path in practice; if most work is instruction-led, the loop CLIs/git hook matter more than the lifecycle hooks.

U3. partially-supported - Jev's sufficiency 0.40 and residual 0.94 are single-sample advisory classifications over a summarized proposal; corroborating, not proof.

U4. unverified - Symlink-based escape of the log directory is not closed by lexical containment; whether to resolve realpath is a follow-up decision.

processAppendix.content:
Triage: DEEP x hybrid. Tracks: T1 deterministic-seam design (lifecycle hooks, loop CLIs, wt-session, trace contract); T2 path/config/migration/dead-code design; host plugin API inspected directly; primary ran prototypes.

Prototypes (sandboxed /tmp/opencode, no repo writes): a `scripts/trace.mjs`-style wrapper over appendTrace/recordDecision wrote 2 redacted UTC lines (action + decision); a lifecycle trace hook fired task-create/task-complete/checkpoint and appended 3 lines [ref-prototypes].

Independent challenger (anti-anchored): F1-F3, F5-F8 upheld with corrections; F4 DOWNGRADED - several 'instruction-only' skills do have code seams (scan/ddd/upload CLIs; bdd-tdd/make-tests libs imported by csm-build; review loop-closure), so the residual is agent-composed/no-CLI steps, not most skills. Citation fixes applied (plan key is risksAndRecovery; appendTrace is sync-returning-a-promise; F5 was already implemented).

Jev advisory (not a gate): a bounded batched call returned fix_who=in_repo_seams (P=0.98), sufficient noul=0.40, residual_gap=instruction_led_skills (P=0.94), and rubric factual 0.64 / completeness 0.99 / clarity 0.83 [ref-jev-review]; the sub-0.7 factual advisory reflects the summarized state and prompted the corrected claims.

VERIFY (primary-personal, never delegated): claims anchored to file:line or declared artifacts; prototypes ran outside the repo; Jev artifact contains no key; protected-state diff limited to this run's finding, artifacts, and progress record. Not committed.

claims.statement: The recording gap is real: only scripts/wt-session.mjs calls appendTrace; recordDecision has no production caller; no hook records ordinary actions.

The minimal automatic seam is the orchestrator lifecycle hook runner: index.mjs already calls hooks?.run(...) at eight fixed points every run, but the handlers are inert because production never supplies lifecycleHooks (run-orchestrator calls orchestrate without it); supplying a built-in trace hook is the smallest deterministic wiring.

The three loop CLIs (csm-build loop-guard, csm-plan loop-evaluator, csm-review loop-closure) are additional deterministic emission points when invoked: each already computes a runId and an outcome and is a documented per-cycle command.

Lifecycle hooks are synchronous while the trace writer returns a promise, so a trace hook must fire-and-forget with a pending-set plus a flush before exit, and use a best-effort dynamic import because the payload mirror has no scripts/ directory.
A new scripts/trace.mjs CLI plus a make trace target is the deterministic sink for explicit and instruction-led use; AGENTS.md should name that exact command instead of a general instruction.

Several skills that look instruction-only do have code seams (csm-scan/csm-ddd/csm-upload CLIs; csm-bdd-tdd and csm-make-tests libs imported by csm-build; csm-review's loop-closure), so the true residual is agent-composed prose/narrative steps and any step that invokes no CLI; a host opencode plugin using tool.execute.after/event/permission.ask is the only seam that covers those universally.

Path hardening: a relative configured traceLogPath can escape the repo root because repoLogPath uses path.join(mainRoot, configured) and join normalizes '..'; contain relative paths under the main root (an escape falls back to the in-repo default). The invalid-layer-to-in-repo-default behavior already exists and only needs correcting in the docs.

Old logs should be left/archived, not auto-migrated: .agents/logs/* is gitignored (operator action) and re-concatenation duplicates lines; document both the old <git-common-dir> log and the legacy per-run file.
The per-run fallback in scripts/wt-session.mjs is unreachable dead code (appendTrace and repoLogPath load in the same try; the null guard returns before the ternary) and should be deleted.

Prototypes verified that a trace CLI wrapper and a lifecycle trace hook both append redacted UTC JSONL; Jev advisory (via a bounded batched call) rates the in-repo seam approach correct (0.98), sufficiency 0.40, and the residual gap as instruction-led skills (0.94) - corroborating, never a gate.
